title: Define the durable Journal contract
goal: Turn durable session recovery into an implementable contract before selecting or adding a storage adapter.
scope: Specify durability, atomicity, ordering, schema-version, recovery, corruption, and concurrent-writer behavior at the Journal port boundary.
Define how storage location, ownership, lifetime, migration, and deletion are selected and exposed to the user.
Identify the kernel consumer scenarios and failure observations needed to verify a future adapter.
Compare proportionate storage approaches against the contract without selecting a technology or path in advance.
acceptance: A reviewed repository document states the durable Journal invariants and typed failure behavior.
The contract defines restart and deliberately malformed-state checks that distinguish unknown, empty, incomplete, and corrupt histories.
The contract defines atomic expected-revision append across supported processes and states the filesystem or service assumptions required for that guarantee.
The design records the selected storage approach and location only after evaluating them against explicit requirements.
The resulting implementation task can proceed without relying on chat context or claiming persistence is already delivered.
context: This task becomes ready only after the task workflow is accepted.
No database, file format, storage path, or migration mechanism has been selected.

history.note: Contract work is planned and waits for completion of DEV-0003.
